FIX A EDIT (verbatim, ADDED as H4 sub-block IMMEDIATELY AFTER the §3.1E 'Cross-references.' line and BEFORE the §3.1F UNION-vs-UNION-ALL header — adjacent to count_if, NOT a rewrite of §3.1E or §11):
  - H4 HEADER: `#### bool_or / bool_and — "did ANY (or did ALL) rows in the group satisfy X?" (roll up a boolean per group)`
  - KEYWORD ANCHORS (single READ-THIS-FIRST block): `did any shipment arrive late`, `did any row in the group satisfy X`, `did all rows satisfy X`, `any true in a group`, `all true in a group`, `roll up a yes/no flag per group`, `bool_or`, `bool_and`, `group boolean any/all`, `at least one row is true`, `every row is true`, `aggregate a boolean per group`, `single true/false per group`, `did any order have a late shipment`, `did every shipment arrive on time`, `boolean aggregation`, `roll up bool`, `collapse boolean per group`. Verified at trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html on 2026-06-07.
  - LEAD (one-fact summary): `bool_or(predicate)` returns TRUE if ANY input value is TRUE, otherwise FALSE; `bool_and(predicate)` returns TRUE if EVERY input value is TRUE, otherwise FALSE. Both ignore NULLs (NOT in count/count_if/max_by/min_by/approx_distinct exception list). Both return single boolean per group.
  - VERBATIM TRINO 467 DOCS QUOTES (WebFetch-verified at trino.io/docs/467/functions/aggregate.html):
     * `bool_or(boolean) -> boolean` — *"Returns TRUE if any input value is TRUE, otherwise FALSE."*
     * `bool_and(boolean) -> boolean` — *"Returns TRUE if every input value is TRUE, otherwise FALSE."*
  - WORKED EXAMPLE (canonical shape — the exact user question):
     `SELECT order_id, bool_or(is_late) AS any_late, bool_and(is_late) AS all_late FROM shipments GROUP BY order_id`
     — any_late = TRUE if at least one shipment was late; all_late = TRUE only if every shipment was late. Predicate form also valid (any boolean expression).
  - VS-NEIGHBORS TABLE (so responder picks bool_or for boolean asks, not count_if/MAX/CASE):
     * 'Did ANY row in group satisfy X? (single TRUE/FALSE)' → bool_or(pred) — docs-canonical, signature returns boolean.
     * 'Did ALL rows in group satisfy X? (single TRUE/FALSE)' → bool_and(pred) — purpose-built 'every row'.
     * 'How many rows satisfied X per group? (a count)' → count_if(pred) per §3.1E LEADING CANONICAL — returns bigint, NOT boolean, different question.
     * 'Is the count > 0 per group?' → count_if(pred) > 0 WORKAROUND (works but indirect: count-then-compare); prefer bool_or(pred).
     * 'Use MAX on a boolean column?' → MAX(bool_col) AVOID; use bool_or instead. Works empirically (boolean orderable, TRUE > FALSE) BUT max(x) signature in Trino aggregate docs does NOT enumerate boolean — only orderable numeric/date/string. bool_or is docs-canonical boolean aggregate.
  - NET RULE: 'a single TRUE/FALSE per group: did ANY satisfy X' → bool_or(pred) is direct, docs-canonical idiom. 'did ALL satisfy X' → bool_and(pred). 'how many satisfied X' (count, not boolean) → count_if(pred) per §3.1E above. DO NOT write count_if(pred) > 0 when you want boolean — write bool_or(pred). DO NOT write MAX(bool_col) when you want boolean — write bool_or(bool_col).
  - OPTIONAL WINDOW NOTE (one line): both work as window functions with OVER(...) — `bool_or(is_late) OVER (PARTITION BY order_id)` returns per-order any-late flag attached to every row without collapsing.
